resources.string: Example board. Playing generates a new random board.
Connect start 0 to extraction 6 and execute turn without losing.
Learn by playing 10 short guided lessons. Practice never changes your match, credits or records. You can exit and resume from the beginning of your last lesson.
Tutorial completed. You can practice again whenever you like.
Follow the highlighted action. Other actions do not change this exercise.

string-array.name: tutorial_instructions
string-array.item: Connect start 0 to extraction 6 with dominoes. Practice is safe: no credits spent, no records changed.
Select the highlighted 0–2 tile. Each tile covers two cells.
Tap the highlighted cell by start. Every touching value must match; the two halves of one tile may differ.
Connected! Place one tile per turn. Occupied cells and firewalls are off limits.
Select 2–0. Its 0 must end up next to start.
Press Rotate: the tile stands vertical.
Rotate again: horizontal with swapped halves. Four rotations loop back to the start.
Place the tile in the highlighted cell. Its 0 matches start.
Execute the turn. Placing a tile first is required. Trace rises by 8 plus pending script noise.
A tile is drawn while the bag lasts, RAM refills to 3, and a script may arrive. Noise resets; trace never drops on its own.
Firewalls block cells. The daemon marches toward start. Traps hide; visible bonuses grant RAM or cut trace.
Select 0–2 to work the two cells beside start.
Place the highlighted tile to grab RAM and cooling. A trap hides in this exercise.
The trap adds 20 noise and discards a script. Execute the turn and watch trace climb.
Cooling removes 8 trace; a reserve grants 1 RAM, capped at 3. Watch trace and the daemon every turn.
Press PING. Costs 1 RAM, adds no noise, previews the next tile and reveals one hidden trap.
Select the 0–2 tile after PING.
Place it beside start to collect the RAM reserve.
Select KILL PROCESS in the same turn. Costs 3 RAM, adds 15 noise.
Tap the revealed honeypot to destroy it before ending the turn.
Execute the turn now that both scripts resolved.
Select SPOOF. On apply it costs 2 RAM and adds 5 noise. It rewrites one half of a tile, 0 to 6.
Select the 1–2 tile to modify.
Choose its second half.
Choose value 3. Nothing is spent yet.
Press Cancel. Tile and resources stay untouched.
Select SPOOF again for a useful change.
Select the 1–2 tile.
Choose the first half, holding 1.
Choose 0 so it can join start.
Press Apply. RAM is spent, noise added, tile rewritten.
Select the modified 0–2 tile.
Place it beside start. SPOOF helps when nothing matches.
Select KILL PROCESS. Costs 3 RAM, adds 15 noise. It clears a firewall, a revealed honeypot, or a whole placed tile. Never the daemon.
Tap the highlighted firewall. Any bridge on it breaks too.
Select 0–2: the blocked cell is free now.
Place the tile in the highlighted cell.
Select BRIDGE. Costs 2 RAM, adds 10 noise. It links across a firewall without removing it, and needs an adjacent tile.
Switch the bridge to horizontal: our line runs left to right.
Tap the highlighted firewall. The bridge carries value 2; occupied ends on both sides must match.
Select 2–6 to continue past the firewall.
Place it in the highlighted cell. Tiles never sit on the firewall itself.
Select 4–6 to finish the route.
Place the highlighted tile: 4 extends the network, 6 touches extraction.
Execute the turn to confirm victory. Stay under 100 trace and keep the daemon away from start.
Victory! You can also lose by hitting 100 trace, letting the daemon reach start, running out of tiles, or having no legal move and no rescue script.
Outside practice, victory pays 20 credits, plus 40 for each challenge\'s first win. Every 5 challenges unlock a free-play scenario.
